annotations.description: Alertmanager has failed to deliver {{ $value | humanize }} notifications/sec over the last 5 minutes (integration={{ $labels.integration }}). Likely causes: ntfy down, basic_auth credential drift (check /etc/alertmanager/ntfy-password vs ntfy user.db), ntfy rate-limit exhaustion (HTTP 429), or network partition on the monitoring Docker network. Triage: `docker logs alertmanager | tail -50` and `docker logs ntfy | tail -50`. Runbook: homelab-infra/docs/ha-replication-runbook.md.

annotations.description: HA resource {{ $labels.sid }} (type {{ $labels.type }}) on node {{ $labels.node }} has state={{ $labels.state }} for >2m. The LRM has either exhausted max_restart retries (error), the node was fenced, or recovery is wedged. Recovery (PVE 9.x): ha-manager set {{ $labels.sid }} --state disabled (NOT --state stopped — rejected on error-state resources) → diagnose root cause via `ssh {{ $labels.node }} 'journalctl -u pve-ha-lrm -n 200'` and /var/log/pve/ha-manager.log.{0,1} → fix underlying issue → ha-manager set {{ $labels.sid }} --state started. Full sequence at runbook_url.
annotations.summary: PVE HA resource {{ $labels.sid }} unhealthy on {{ $labels.node }} (state={{ $labels.state }})

annotations.description: HA resource {{ $labels.sid }} on node {{ $labels.node }} has been in transient state {{ $labels.state }} for >2m. Transient states normally clear in seconds (~30s upper bound). Check `ssh {{ $labels.node }} 'ha-manager status'` and `journalctl -u pve-ha-crm -u pve-ha-lrm -n 200`. Common causes: wedged CRM tick, stuck migration, pmxcfs lock contention.
annotations.summary: PVE HA resource {{ $labels.sid }} stuck in transient state {{ $labels.state }} on {{ $labels.node }}

annotations.description: Node {{ $labels.node }} reports HA quorum=0 for >1m. With softdog armed (Story 6.3), nodes that lose quorum will self-fence within ~60s of the watchdog timer expiring. Immediate operator action: check corosync ring health (`corosync-cfgtool -s`), inspect `journalctl -u corosync -n 200`, restore connectivity. See homelab-infra/docs/ha-replication-runbook.md.
annotations.summary: PVE HA quorum lost on {{ $labels.node }}

annotations.description: sum(pve_ha_master) = {{ $value }} for >2m. Expected: exactly 1 (single master cluster-wide). 0 = no master elected (CRM cannot make decisions); >1 = split-brain (multiple masters disagreeing). Check `ssh pveN 'ha-manager status'` on each node — every node should report the same master in the `master` line.
annotations.summary: PVE HA master missing or split (sum(pve_ha_master)={{ $value }}, expected 1)

annotations.description: Node {{ $labels.node }}'s LRM is not in `active` status for >2m. Check `ssh {{ $labels.node }} 'ha-manager status'` to see the actual status (idle / wait_for_agent_lock / lost_agent_lock / maintenance). LRM not active means this node cannot start or stop HA resources — failovers TO this node will fail. Restart with `systemctl restart pve-ha-lrm` if stuck.
annotations.summary: PVE HA LRM not active on {{ $labels.node }}

annotations.description: `pve_ha_exporter_last_run_timestamp_seconds` has no sample for at least one of pve1/pve2/pve3 for >5m. Check `curl -s http://<node>:9100/metrics | grep pve_ha_` on each PVE host. Known-good state: 3 samples (one per node).

annotations.description: The sum of pve_replication_exporter_jobs_total across all pve nodes is less than 8. Expected: pve1=4 + pve2=0 + pve3=4 = 8. A silent drop means a job was deleted, the exporter errored out, or pvesh returned an empty array. Inspect `pvesh get /nodes/<node>/replication` on each PVE host and compare to §"Current replication matrix" in homelab-infra/docs/ha-replication-runbook.md.

annotations.description: Job {{ $labels.jobid }} (source {{ $labels.source }} → target {{ $labels.target }}) reports OK with fail_count=0 but hasn't synced in >1h. Despite the rule name this does NOT query zfs directly — it flags the pvesr state-machine disagreeing with its own timestamps. Operator check: `ssh {{ $labels.target }} "zfs list -t snapshot -r rpool/data | grep __replicate_{{ $labels.jobid }}"` to confirm whether the latest target-side snapshot is actually fresh. If zfs shows a recent __replicate_ snapshot, pvesr bookkeeping is out of sync (run `pvesr run --id {{ $labels.jobid }} --verbose`); if not, the cycle really did stall.
annotations.summary: Possible silent-stall replication for {{ $labels.jobid }} on {{ $labels.node }} (name retained as 'SnapshotOrphan' for symmetry with runbook)
